newsitem.title: MEXICO: FORECAST - Cemex Q1 seen lackluster.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Cemex Q1 seen lackluster.

text.p: Mexican-based Cemex SA on Friday is expected to post lackluster first-quarter results that reflect a slow economic recovery, analysts said.
"The much-anticipated recovery in Cemex's operations did not materialize. All areas are down, but in our view better times are ahead," New York Bear Stearns analyst Sobani Warner said in a report.

Ten industry analysts on average estimated earnings of 0.918 pesos a share for the quarter, compared with 2.40 pesos for the same period the previous year. The estimates ranged between 0.70 peso and 1.29 pesos.

Consolidated revenue is estimated at 6.439 billion pesos, or an increase of less than one percent in real terms. The company's operating margin is forecast at about 21.9 percent, less than the 25.2 percent realised in the first quarter of 1996.

Cemex's Mexican unit is seen as less profitable because of low prices, although analysts estimated an increase of between six and 10 percent in tonnage sold compared with the first three months of 1996, when output was 3.0 million.
"Continued price competition and higher production costs are expected to have further narrowed the Mexican operating margin," JP Morgan analyst Eric Linder said in a report.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell Mexico City analyst Gordon Lee said Cemex's Mexico operations were still stronger than the competition.
Uglow estimated cement prices of about $76 per tonne, compared with $74 per tonne in the fourth quarter of 1996. Other analysts estimated no change in cement prices from the fourth quarter.
The Spanish unit is also expected to report weak earnings amid stagnant demand and after the devaluation of the peseta versus the dollar, analysts said.
Analysts said attention was focused on Cemex operations in Venezuela and Colombia, which will consolidate cement and ready-mix producer Industrias Samper for the first time.
